FINANCIALS.title: Official financial reconciliation
FINANCIALS.text: The June 2026 consolidated statements use thousand TRY at June purchasing power. Financial debt is TRY 68.201bn; excluding blocked cash and deducting financial investments gives net debt of −TRY 102.232bn. Presentation cash uses a broader definition. Primary documents were reconciled; no second independent data source was established.

HISTORY.title: Five-year comparison
HISTORY.text: Official 2021–2025 reports were located. 2021 sales were TRY 150.972bn originally and TRY 152.492bn in the 2022 comparative. The 2023–2025 reports also use different year-end purchasing-power bases. Full scope and restatement reconciliation remains missing; no common-basis growth series was generated.

DIVIDEND.title: Dividend sustainability
DIVIDEND.text: KAP approved gross TRY 17.1268815/share and net TRY 14.5578492 with 15% withholding. Ex and payment dates differ; the schedule is not independent settlement evidence. H1 operating cash of TRY 132.366bn minus asset purchases of TRY 11.858bn equals TRY 120.508bn. Working capital contributed TRY 28.497bn and derivative cash classification needs normalization. This is not sustainable FCF. Full history and cash coverage are missing; 10/15/20-year backtests remain blocked.

VALUATION.title: Why refining valuation remains open
VALUATION.text: The October presentation reports H1 refining margin of USD 15.6/bbl and capex of USD 246m; annual capex of USD 700m is guidance. Inventory effects and exceptional margins are not normalized earnings. A sourced annual normalized EBITDA bridge, consistent net debt, current shares and peer multiple are missing. No bear/base/bull price was produced. Formula: (normalized EBITDA × multiple − net debt) / shares. FCF, BOOK_ROE, NAV and DDM implementations remain pending.

TECHNICAL.title: Price and volume coverage
TECHNICAL.text: Independently reconciled daily price, volume, corporate-action and FX data are missing. SMA20/50/200, RSI, MACD and support/resistance were not calculated. Prior price snapshots are not live prices.

DISCLOSURES.title: Disclosure coverage limit
DISCLOSURES.text: Earlier KAP events and sources are retained. This review does not establish full coverage of 11–22 October 2026 or previously unread attachments. An issuer KAP filing and its investor presentation are not two independent economic sources.

FINANCIALS.title: Primary financial reconciliation
FINANCIALS.text: 14 key rows match KAP #1643116 and the issuer’s H1 2026 report. Thousand TRY was converted to TRY, preserving consolidated scope and 30 June 2026 purchasing power. Financial debt is TRY 68.20bn; net cash under the issuer’s note definition is TRY 102.23bn. TRY 28.49bn of total cash is blocked. This match is not an independent review.

HISTORY.title: Five-year documents and basis differences
HISTORY.text: Revenue, parent profit/equity, operating cash, debt and unblocked cash are available for 2021–2025. 2021 uses the restated 2022 column following the Entek combination. 2023–2025 annual changes use comparable columns in the same report. A single purchasing-power basis for all five years remains unavailable.

DIVIDEND.title: Cash coverage and historical-data limits
DIVIDEND.text: 2025 operating cash of TRY 49.46bn less TRY 19.12bn capex leaves TRY 30.35bn, versus TRY 34.84bn cash dividends on the same basis. Operating cash covers distributions 1.42 times; the post-capex proxy does not fully cover them. This does not automatically predict a cut. The 2026 payment schedule and 2023 600% bonus record were located; full historical settlement, price and FX coverage remain unverified. None of the 10/15/20-year backtests is complete. MKK #1671443 records the second instalment as settled on 2 October 2026 at a gross rate of 674.69533% (TRY 6.7469533/share). This is custodian evidence for one event, not an independent review of the full history.

VALUATION.title: Refining cycle; no target price
VALUATION.text: The issuer reports H1 2026 net refining margin of USD 15.6/bbl, with Q1 at 9.4 and Q2 at 21.4. Such volatility cautions against treating one strong quarter as permanent earnings. Full-year margin guidance of USD 13–15/bbl and USD 700m capex are plans, not realized results. A verified multi-year normalized EBITDA bridge addressing inventory/working-capital effects and comparable peer multiples is still missing. No bear/base/bull price targets were produced.

TECHNICAL.title: Price and volume verification missing
TECHNICAL.text: The market series has not been reconciled with an official session calendar and independent raw price/volume history. TCMB indicative USD buying/selling rates on 9 October 2026 are 49.1274/49.2160; these are not market closing rates. One sample does not verify 20 years of FX. No new SMA20/50/200, RSI, MACD or support/resistance outputs were produced without validated inputs.

researchTuprs.name: Tüpraş
researchTuprs.headline: Strong operating momentum; durability needs testing
researchTuprs.summary: Refining analysis depends on product-to-crude spreads, utilisation and working capital more than the direction of oil prices alone. This report takes a dividend perspective without treating short-term profits as sustainable earnings. Financial strength and prospective shareholder returns are separate questions.
researchTuprs.strengths: Operating margin and current ratio are reproducible. The cash buffer is a useful starting point for assessing resilience to weaker margins, but cash on the balance sheet is not automatically distributable profit.
researchTuprs.risks: Normalising product margins, inventory valuation, derivative settlements and new investments can change cash generation. Past dividends do not commit the company to future payouts.
researchTuprs.accounting: Consolidated TAS 34 interim report, in 30 June 2026 purchasing power. Source amounts in thousands of TRY were multiplied by 1,000. H1 2025 comparisons use the restated column in the same report. Six-month earnings were not annualised.
researchTuprs.cashQuality: Operating cash less capex is insufficient as a measure of cash available for distribution. Derivative settlements and interest classified under financing need separate review. This difference is therefore not used directly for dividend coverage or DCF.
researchTuprs.growth: Revenue and parent profit are compared across matching half-years. Extrapolating profit growth in a straight line could miss the refining cycle. Production volumes, margins and returns on reinvestment should be assessed together.
researchTuprs.peers: Peer refinery valuations on comparable periods and accounting bases are incomplete. No sector-average multiple or peer discount is asserted.
researchTuprs.dividend: The KAP shareholder approval specifies two 2026 instalments totalling TRY 17.1268815 gross per share. Ex-dates: 16 March and 30 September; scheduled account payment dates: 18 March and 2 October. This is the approved timetable, not verification of receipt in a personal account.
researchTuprs.sustainability: The displayed ratio divides the approved annual gross dividend by the 9 October reference price. It is not the future return available to a new buyer. Sustainability requires through-cycle cash flow, investment needs, debt maturities and legal distribution capacity.
researchTuprs.valuation: A sourced price is available, but normalised earnings, justified peer multiples and forward cash-flow assumptions are incomplete. No discount/fair/premium label or target price is produced. Market capitalisation and book value below are descriptive calculations only.

methods.pe: Applicable to refining, but peak-cycle earnings may produce a misleadingly low P/E. Normalised annual EPS and justified peer multiples are missing. Doubling half-year earnings does not resolve this; no valuation result.
methods.ev: Helps separate operations from financing. Comparable normalised EBITDA, peer multiples and the net debt/minority/associate bridge are required. Cash less debt alone is not a complete enterprise-value bridge; no valuation result.
methods.dcf: Models investment and cash conversion explicitly. Multi-year volumes, margins, tax, capex, working capital, WACC and terminal growth are missing. Nominal TRY cash flows must not be discounted at a real rate; no valuation result.

researchTuprs.scenarios: These are research conditions, not numerical price targets. Probabilities, discount rates and normalised cash flows do not yet support bear/base/bull values. At a fixed P/E, a percentage change in normalised EPS changes model price by the same percentage; this mathematical sensitivity is not an earnings forecast.

scenarioNotes.bear: Lower refining margins with sustained investment and working-capital needs could constrain distributions.
scenarioNotes.base: Margins move toward a cycle average and investment stays within budget. The cycle average is not yet verified.
scenarioNotes.bull: Strong product margins persist and investments deliver expected cash contributions. These outcomes are not assumed.

researchTuprs.technical: The five-session average is a short price summary, not a confirmed trend or buy signal. Adjusted history is insufficient for RSI/MACD, long averages and volume confirmation. Longer series crossing dividend dates require adjustment checks. These calculations are not total returns.
researchTuprs.scanLimit: The company KAP list and selected direct disclosures were examined for 11 July–11 October. A headline scan is not a completed content review. July rating/bonds, August redemption, September insurance and some attachments remain outstanding. Share sale, Entek contribution, margin revision and debt decision/application were reviewed. No claim is made that other material disclosures are absent.
researchTuprs.riskFollowup: Next checks should cover approval/issuance after the debt application, Entek’s external spending and earnings contribution, share-sale disclosures, delivery against margin guidance and dividend payment confirmations. Incomplete KAP coverage does not support a low news-risk conclusion.
researchTuprs.history: First report; no previous-version comparison exists. A new instruction creates a separate version, preserving earlier sources and inputs. Research files do not change watchlist membership or portfolio transactions.
researchTuprs.review: Research and review were performed in the same Codex session, not independently. Identity and used inputs are sourced; decimal arithmetic makes calculations reproducible. Outstanding KAP content/attachments, peer valuation, normalised earnings, cash-flow adjustments and long technical history leave the outcome NEEDS_REVIEW. This is partial research.

education.debtLong: Financial obligations classified beyond one year. A long maturity does not imply low interest or currency risk; denomination and contract terms matter.

researchTuprs.debtMeaning: Debt due within one year includes both short-term facilities and approaching instalments of long-term loans. Compare it with operating cash, unrestricted liquidity and refinancing access. Longer maturities reduce immediate pressure but do not remove interest or refinancing risk.

This limited review also cannot establish the absence of political connections. Ownership, past privatisation or public-sector business alone do not prove political alignment.
company.exposure: Analyst interpretation: sanctions and regional conflict can affect crude supply, freight/insurance costs and refining margins. Tax, energy and environmental policy changes can affect demand, investment and cash flow. Higher country risk can raise financing costs and reduce market multiples. Effects are not one-directional and require event-specific official/KAP review.
company.limit: This is not a comprehensive political-connections investigation. No verified party affiliation or targeted political action is established here; transmission channels are scenarios. No percentage price effect or target is attributed to a political event.

longTerm.verdict: A conditional candidate for a long-term dividend research shortlist.
longTerm.assessment: I consider Tüpraş worth researching over 10–15 years: refining can generate cash and new energy investments could diversify earnings. Suitability for steadily rising annual income is not established. My constructive view depends on investment returns and preserving dividend capacity through weak refining cycles. It does not establish that today’s price is attractive.
longTerm.confidence: Limited research confidence: an adjusted 10–15-year dividend, earnings and cash-flow series and interruption history are incomplete. The horizon is approximately 2036–2041; a 2035 corporate plan does not substantiate the entire period. Time does not eliminate uncertainty.
longTerm.durability: Refining and energy needs support the thesis, but demand, competition and environmental costs can change. Existing plants do not guarantee strong earnings for fifteen years. New investment must be assessed against possible erosion in the legacy business.
longTerm.income: Supportive policy, variable cash income. Refining cycles and major investments can reduce or interrupt dividends. I would not treat distributions as fixed payments for recurring expenses.
longTerm.entry: Price still matters over long horizons. An excellent transition story bought at an excessive price can deliver poor returns. Current P/B and earnings scenarios are informative, but do not establish a discounted entry.
longTerm.payout: The official policy uses 80% of net distributable profit when conditions permit. This does not mean an 80% return on invested money. Payout ratio = dividends / distributable profit; dividend yield = dividend per share / share price. Future distributions depend on earnings, cash, investment and shareholder approval. The report’s 4.43% is a historical/approved distribution divided by a reference price, not next year’s yield.
longTerm.allocation: Retained cash can grow future earnings and dividends if invested productively. Overpriced or unsuccessful projects can damage both. A high payout is not sufficient: assess cash remaining after maintenance, growth investment and debt service.
longTerm.realReturn: A rising TRY dividend can still lose purchasing power; inflation and foreign-currency comparisons matter. Total return includes net distributions and share-value changes. Reinvestment can increase share count, but tax, fees, purchase prices and business outcomes matter. No fifteen-year return percentage is generated from assumed inputs.
longTerm.fit: Potentially relevant for investors able to tolerate variable distributions and price declines while reviewing the business. Poor fit for guaranteed or fixed annual income. Single-company income remains concentrated over long horizons; no personal allocation is proposed.
longTerm.growthIntro: Three opportunities merit monitoring. Plans below are company disclosures; earnings and valuation implications are conditional analysis. Sector expansion alone does not create shareholder value without profitable projects, sound financing and timely execution.

saf.title: Sustainable aviation fuel · SAF
saf.evidence: The company disclosed a new İzmir SAF facility plan and a long-term feedstock agreement. These steps do not establish full commercial operation.
saf.upside: Developing low-carbon aviation demand could add sales and diversify products. Integration with refining creates value only if it supports competitive costs and cash earnings.
saf.proof: Commissioning, certification, customer contracts, sustainable feedstock costs and positive post-investment cash contribution.
saf.risk: Feedstock inflation, certification/construction delays and competition compressing premiums. Sales growth need not translate into equivalent profit growth.

electricity.title: Renewable / zero-carbon electricity
electricity.evidence: The company plans to grow its electricity portfolio through Entek and integrate generation with new energy activities.
electricity.upside: External sales can diversify income; competitively priced power can support internal operations. More balanced cash generation could reduce refining-cycle dependence.
electricity.proof: Commissioned capacity, actual production, realised prices, grid access and returns exceeding financing costs.
electricity.risk: Low power prices, weather, grid limits and expensive debt. Internally consumed electricity must not be counted twice as both external revenue and full savings.

hydrogen.title: Green hydrogen
hydrogen.evidence: The company reports completed engineering for a pilot electrolyser, targeting installation in 2028–2030 and integration with SAF.
hydrogen.upside: Competitive production costs could support low-carbon operations and future customers. I treat this as long-term optionality rather than certain earnings today.
hydrogen.proof: Pilot costs and efficiency, competitive electricity, credible customer demand and a commercial-scale investment decision.
hydrogen.risk: Technology costs, subsidy dependence, weak demand and delays. Pilot success does not establish profitable large-scale production.

longTerm.pricing: Additional value can come from sustainable cash growth per share or a higher market multiple for more stable earnings. Expectations may already be priced in. Announced investments are not automatically added to valuation: capital spending, financing, tax and legacy-business erosion must be considered.
longTerm.confirm: Projects commissioned within budget, demonstrable cash contributions, dividends funded by operations after maintenance/growth investment, and manageable debt/FX pressure. A share-price decline alone does not strengthen the thesis.
longTerm.invalidate: Persistently weak refining economics, repeated delays and overruns, debt growing without cash generation, recurring asset sales or borrowing to fund dividends, and poor minority-shareholder capital allocation. A temporary dividend cut for productive investment differs from permanent business deterioration.

monitor.quarter: Each financial report: refining margin, operating and available cash, debt maturities and capital expenditure—not just net profit.
monitor.year: Annually: real growth in net dividend per share, cash coverage, realised project returns and current valuation.
monitor.event: Reassess after major investments/financing, sanctions, production outages, capital actions or dividend-policy changes. This is a review plan; the application does not monitor automatically.
monitor.missing: Evidence still needed: split-adjusted 10–15-year dividend and interruption history, through-cycle free cash flow, project costs/returns and peer valuation. These gaps prevent an unconditional fifteen-year holding conclusion.

researchDoas.name: Dogus Otomotiv
researchDoas.headline: Profitability is shrinking, the TUVTURK exit is under way; a firm verdict is premature without 9M26
researchDoas.summary: For an automotive distributor, what matters is not manufacturer profit but FX risk (imported cost base vs. TRY sales), the ÖTV/tax regime, and unit volume. This report covers both the dividend and cyclical/growth angle; a single quarter's profit is not automatically sustainable earnings. Financial strength and expected share return are assessed separately.
researchDoas.strengths: A regular, frequent (1-2 instalments a year) dividend record and high trading volume in the free float. Two separate gross TRY 15/share payments were made in 2026. If the TUVTURK stake sale completes (price not yet disclosed) it could bring in cash and reduce debt.
researchDoas.risks: An ongoing profitability decline through 2025-2026 (FY2025 net profit -68%, H1 2026 net profit -35% YoY), rising net debt/EBITDA (1.8x to 2.2x, March-June 2026), and falling sales volume and market share. FX risk (imported vehicle cost) and ÖTV/tax changes directly affect margin.
researchDoas.accounting: Consolidated interim figures under TAS 29 (inflation accounting). The company's primary "Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements" PDFs dated 30.06.2026 and 31.03.2026 (via the investor-relations site) were read directly: both state explicitly that amounts are presented at the purchasing power of their own balance-sheet date (30 June 2026 / 31 March 2026 respectively). The 2025 first-half and first-quarter comparisons come from the same primary report's comparative column, on the same purchasing-power basis; the six-month profit was not annualized. Annualization appears only as an explicitly labelled hypothetical scenario (see peRunRate). Revenue, net profit (parent share), operating profit, equity and balance-sheet items are verified against these primary documents; EBITDA (ebitdaH1) and the FY2025 full-year figures still rest on secondary sources.
researchDoas.cashQuality: The primary H1 2026 report's cash flow statement (p.10) was read: despite a net profit of TRY 2,356,360 thousand, operating cash flow for H1 2026 was NEGATIVE at TRY (2,677,424) thousand (H1 2025: TRY (12,728,764) thousand, also negative but deeper). Most of the net profit did not convert to cash, due to a rise in working capital (inventory, trade receivables) and tax/provision payments. The simple FCF proxy (operating cash minus tangible capex) is therefore also negative (cashProxy). This directly shows profit is not matching cash generation; dividend-paying capacity this period is likely being funded from borrowing or existing cash rather than operating cash - the exact mechanism cannot be stated without examining the financing section (C.).
researchDoas.cashBridge: The company's own Note 25 definition in the primary document: TRY 33.739782bn financial debt − 1.512478bn cash excluding blocked deposits = TRY 32.227304bn net financial debt (0.43x equity). Unlike TUPRS, this definition does not net financial investments (TRY 3.777774bn, Note 6) out of the debt figure; doing so would bring it down to TRY 28.449530bn - this is not an adjustment we made, it is the company's own reported figure. Working capital was a TRY 2.473845bn DRAG on cash in H1 2026 (not a contribution, unlike TUPRS), driven by rising inventory and trade receivables; this direction can reverse and should not be expected to recur every year. Operating cash minus capex is not normalized FCF; financing-section borrowing and dividend flows require separate review.
researchDoas.growth: Revenue and net profit were compared over the same half-year / quarterly periods. In Q1 2026 the total market was -3%, DOAS -2%; in Q2 2026 wholesale volume (excluding Skoda) was -14%, with a first-half market share of 14.3% (third place, behind Stellantis and Renault). The operating expense ratio rose from 5.7% to 7.9%, compressing the EBITDA margin. This is a narrowing trend and should not be extrapolated in a straight line.
researchDoas.peers: FROTO (Ford Otosan): P/E 10.11, EV/EBITDA 8.45 (2026-10-26). TOASO (Tofas) P/E and EV/EBITDA were noted from secondary sources at roughly ~10.5 / ~6.7 but without primary verification, so they were not added to this report's facts/calculations. OTKAR data could not be found. DOAS is a distributor while FROTO/TOASO are manufacturers - given the business-model difference, no direct cheap/expensive comparison is drawn.
researchDoas.dividend: Two instalments in 2026: 13 April (ex-date) / 15 April (payment), gross TRY 15.00/share; 13 August (ex-date) / 17 August (payment), gross TRY 15.00/share. Total gross TRY 30.00/share. Investing.com's dividend calendar and Yahoo Finance's DOAS.IS event list corroborate each other. These are decision dates; this report does not confirm payment into any personal account.
researchDoas.sustainability: A dividend was paid in 4 of the last 5 years and a large share of profit was distributed (per a third-party source, roughly 74%). Since profitability narrowed in 2025-2026, this high payout ratio is not guaranteed to continue - the next dividend decision will depend on whether profitability improves or worsens. Sustainability cannot be fully assessed without a cash flow statement (see cashQuality).
researchDoas.valuation: A sourced price and multiples exist; but a genuine TTM earnings series (9M26 missing), a cash flow statement, and a suitable distributor-peer valuation were not completed. We do not produce a "discounted/fair/premium" verdict or a target price. Market capitalization, P/B and two P/E scenarios below are purely descriptive calculations.

methods.pe: Applicable to automotive distribution, but a single quarter/half-year profit swing (FX gains/losses, inventory valuation) can be misleading. True TTM (July 2025-June 2026) profit = FY2025 net profit - H1 2025 net profit + H1 2026 net profit = 3,140 - 3,603 + 2,356 ≈ 1,893 million TRY (the difference between three sourced period figures; this is not kept as a separate entry in this engine because the calculation infrastructure only supports ratios derived from a single raw fact). Market cap / 1,893 ≈ 15.7x - this should be read against the peHalfYear (12.6x, not annualized) and peRunRate (6.3x, naive x2 assumption) figures shown here; each tells a different story and none is the final word on its own.
methods.ev: Enterprise value (market cap + net debt) is divided by operating profitability (EBITDA); this isolates operating performance from capital structure. Because this engine produces market cap as a calculation result, it cannot be used as a second input to EV/EBITDA - so EV/EBITDA is shown here as a separate, manual calculation: EV ≈ TRY 29,656 million (market cap) + TRY 32,227 million (June 2026 net debt) = TRY 61,883 million; on FY2025 EBITDA (TRY 14,717 mn) ≈ 4.2x, on a derived TTM EBITDA (~TRY 12,150 mn, from low-precision secondary data) ≈ 5.1x. This looks lower than peers (FROTO 8.45x) but is not directly comparable given the business-model difference.
methods.dcf: Explicitly models investment and cash conversion. Multi-year volume/margin, tax, capex, working capital, WACC and terminal growth could not be sourced in this session; no result is computed.

researchDoas.scenarios: The following are not numeric target prices but conditions to investigate. For a bear/base/bull fair-value range, probability, discount rate and normalized cash flow are not yet supported.

scenarioNotes.bear: If the decline in sales volume and market share continues and net debt/EBITDA keeps rising, dividend-paying capacity could narrow.
scenarioNotes.base: Margin compression slows in 9M26, the TUVTURK sale completes at a reasonable price, and net debt stabilizes.
scenarioNotes.bull: The 2026 target (117,000 units sold) is met and second-half profitability exceeds the first half. These conditions are not assumed to occur.

researchDoas.technical: No reliable price chart/indicator source was accessed in this report - technical analysis is NOT APPLIED. Only the 52-week range (TRY 125.80-211.19, see the education note on the source conflict) is known; this is a simple observation, not a signal.
researchDoas.scanLimit: For the 27 July-27 October 2026 window, only secondary news sites/financial portals were scanned; the direct KAP detailed-query interface was not reached. Disclosure IDs and direct KAP URLs could not be verified. The TUVTURK stake sale, the Q2 2026 results release and the dividend payments were reviewed. "No other material disclosure" cannot be concluded.
researchDoas.riskFollowup: In the next update, check: the 9M26 financial statement (09 Nov 2026), the TUVTURK sale price and closing conditions, whether the net debt/EBITDA trend continues, sales volume/market share developments, and the cash flow statement. While the KAP scan is PARTIAL, news risk cannot be called low.
researchDoas.history: First report; no prior version to compare against.
researchDoas.review: Research and review were carried out by the same agent, in a separate pass; this is not an independent audit. Identity and the inputs used are linked to sources, and market cap was cross-checked two ways (price x shares, and back out of P/B). Because KAP content/attachment coverage, the cash flow statement, a suitable peer valuation and a genuine TTM profit series are missing, the review status is NEEDS_REVIEW; this is a partial report.

tuvturk.title: All of the TUVTURK Kuzey and Guney stakes are being sold
tuvturk.fact: A 13 October 2026 board decision, a 16 October letter of intent, and a 19 October KAP disclosure: DOAS is selling its entire 33.333% stake in both TUVTURK Kuzey (capital TRY 510.15 mn, nominal TRY 170.05 mn sold) and TUVTURK Guney (capital TRY 291.246 mn, nominal TRY 97.082 mn sold) to the Turka First/Second Region vehicle inspection companies. The price and final terms have not yet been disclosed.
tuvturk.effect: A full exit from a business line held since 2007. Because the price is undetermined, the cash flow/net debt impact cannot yet be quantified. If completed, this could be read as a strategic refocus toward distribution/EV charging infrastructure; that is an interpretation, not a settled outcome.

dividend.title: 2026's second dividend instalment was paid
dividend.fact: A second instalment, ex-date 13 August, payment 17 August, gross TRY 15.00/share, was distributed (in addition to the first, 13/15 April 2026, gross TRY 15.00/share).
dividend.effect: The publication date falls within the review window. Total gross dividends for 2026 reached TRY 30.00/share; this is not a commitment for future dividends.

q2Results.title: Q2 2026 results: the profitability decline continues
q2Results.fact: An Is Yatirim report dated 20 August: Q2 2026 net profit TRY 1,742 mn (YoY -38%, above expectations), net debt rose to TRY 32,227 mn at end-June 2026 (end-March 2026: TRY 29,516 mn), and net debt/EBITDA rose from 1.8x to 2.2x.
q2Results.effect: Even though profitability beat expectations, the YoY decline and rising leverage should be read together; this does not mean a single positive surprise has reversed the structural trend.

researchDoas.interestMeaning: The debt's interest type (fixed/floating) and effective rates could not be sourced in this session. guide.verdict: A distributor with shrinking profitability and rising leverage, priced at a low P/B and EV/EBITDA; there is not yet enough evidence to call this price "cheap."
guide.reason: A good company and a fair price are not the same thing. The ratios below show the price's relationship to profit and equity. But without a verified genuine TTM earnings series (9M26 missing), a cash flow statement and a suitable distributor peer group, a low-looking multiple is not a reason to buy. This assessment is based on the 27 October 2026 price and 30 June 2026 financials.
guide.business: The decline in sales volume and market share, and margin pressure, are not supportive. The decision to fully exit TUVTURK could be a strategic refocus signal, but its cash impact cannot be assessed until the price is known.
guide.price: P/B (0.40x) and EV/EBITDA (4.2-5.1x) look lower than peers, but the distributor-versus-manufacturer business-model difference weakens the direct comparison. P/E ranges widely across three bases (6.3x-15.7x), which signals real uncertainty about the next 12 months' profitability.
guide.decision: My reading for now: the price's fairness is unclear. Calling it "discounted" or "premium" would be premature before the 9M26 report (9 November 2026) and the TUVTURK sale price are known. If profitability stabilizes and net debt/EBITDA falls, the low multiples could become a more convincing discount signal.
guide.missingIntro: Fair value is an estimate of the cash a company can generate in the future and the risk attached to that cash. Being able to compute a ratio is one thing; justifying what level that ratio should sit at is another. What is missing is not just a formula:

missing.earnings: 1. Sustainable annual earnings: without the 9M26 report, a genuine TTM net profit cannot be completed; the naive x2 annualization (an assumption disproved by FY2025 data) does not resolve seasonality.
missing.benchmark: 2. A suitable comparison: peer multiples on the same business model (distributor, not manufacturer) and the same period/accounting basis could not be found in this session; FROTO/TOASO are manufacturers and are not directly comparable.
missing.cashflow: 3. A cash flow statement: operating cash, capex and working-capital change could not be sourced in this session; how closely net profit tracks cash is unknown.

guide.next: Once these inputs are complete (the 9M26 report, a cash flow statement, distributor peers), a bear/base/bull fair-value range can be computed. The current "cannot be assessed" conclusion does not mean the company is bad; it means we cannot yet prove the price discount.

researchYggyo.name: Yeni Gimat REIT
researchYggyo.headline: Net cash, 99.9% occupancy and a steadily growing dividend - but the price sits 62% above Net Asset Value
researchYggyo.summary: For REITs the key anchor is Net Asset Value (NAV), because investment properties are already carried at fair value. This report covers NAV, the debt/cash structure and the dividend history; a price that trades at a premium to NAV does not mean the company is low quality - it only means the market is paying above today's appraised value.
researchYggyo.strengths: A net cash position (+TRY 2.48 billion, 30.06.2026), wide headroom against all CMB portfolio limits (borrowing ratio 0.11%, limit 500%), 99.9% store occupancy at ANKAmall, an uninterrupted and growing dividend since 2014 (TRY 7.00 and TRY 10.55 per share in the last two years), and operating cash flow (TRY 1.74 billion, H1 2026) running about 3.8x net income (TRY 461 million).
researchYggyo.risks: The price sits 62% above NAV (the reverse of the discount REITs typically trade at); the hotel building has been closed to guests since 16.01.2026 under a regulatory requirement (its rental income is suspended); in September 2026 the wholly owned subsidiary PROEN received a TRY 650 million capital injection into renewable energy (a possible shift in focus); at least 8 circuit-breaker notices were triggered during the period (high volatility/low liquidity); the portfolio is concentrated in one region (Ankara) and one asset (ANKAmall plus hotel).
researchYggyo.accounting: Consolidated interim figures under TAS 29 (high-inflation accounting). The company's primary 30.06.2026 "Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements and Limited Review Report" PDF (via the investor-relations site) was read directly: amounts are presented at 30 June 2026 purchasing power, and the 31.12.2025/H1 2025 comparative columns were ALSO restated to the SAME (June 2026) purchasing power - so the H1 2026 vs H1 2025 comparison is a genuine real comparison. The FY2025 full-year figure (on its own 31.12.2025 basis) is in a different measuring unit; no conversion coefficient between the two bases could be sourced, so TTM was not computed (see education.profitH1Previous).
researchYggyo.cashQuality: The primary H1 2026 report's cash flow statement (p.7) was read: period net income was TRY 461,373,611 while cash flow from operating activities was TRY 1,741,774,649 - real cash generation is about 3.8x the reported accounting profit. The gap is not coincidental: the Net Monetary Gain/(Loss) (TRY 1,165,113,071) and deferred tax expense (TRY 374,058,220) that depress net income are not cash outflows, just effects of TAS 29/tax accounting. Real cash-generating power is much stronger than reported net income.

guide.verdict: A quality, low-debt REIT with high occupancy; but the price is 62% above Net Asset Value - the reverse of the discount typically seen in the sector. A good company and a fair price are not the same thing.
guide.reason: NAV is the most direct valuation anchor for REITs because the real estate is already carried at fair value. A price above NAV means the market is paying more than today's appraised value; whether that is justified (a liquidity premium, future growth expectations, or simple overvaluation) cannot be told apart from this report alone. This assessment is based on the 29 October 2026 price and the 30 June 2026 financials.
guide.business: A net-cash position, 99.9% mall occupancy and a growing dividend are supportive. The hotel renovation and the PROEN energy investment are two open questions; neither outcome is verifiable yet.
guide.price: The 62% NAV premium survives a ±20% hypothetical shock to the real-estate value (even the worst case stays at a premium) - so the result is not overly sensitive to a single appraisal assumption; it shows the stock genuinely trades at a premium.
guide.decision: My current reading: the price is at a premium to NAV, which is not a buy/sell call. A clear directional change should not be expected before the year-end 2026 appraisal and the return on the PROEN investment become clear.

researchTtrak.name: Turk Traktor
researchTtrak.headline: Market leader, low debt - but a 2026 cyclical collapse: a 789.3 million TL loss in 9 months
researchTtrak.summary: This report uses P/B and EV/EBITDA, the methods appropriate for an industrial/automotive company (instead of the REIT NAV approach). The company is net-debt-positive and currently loss-making, so P/E cannot be computed. The assessment tries to separate a cyclical trough from genuine overvaluation, without issuing a firm verdict.
researchTtrak.strengths: Market leadership (a Koc Holding/CNH Industrial joint venture), a long and generally growing dividend history (regular since 2007), low/moderate leverage (far below the CMB borrowing-limit ratio), export sales up +13% partly offsetting the domestic collapse, strong (but largely one-off, inventory-drawdown-driven) operating cash flow (+5.02 billion TL) in 9M2026 despite the net loss.
researchTtrak.risks: Turkey's tractor market shrank 44% in the first 9 months of 2026; domestic sales -51%, production -30%; operating profit swung to a loss (margin -2.34%); JCR downgraded the credit rating from AAA(tr) to AA(tr); TL borrowing cost is 33.79% (Turkey's very high policy-rate environment); the share price fell 37% over the past year; no 2026 dividend payment record was found.
researchTtrak.accounting: Standalone (no consolidated subsidiary), interim figures under TAS 29 (high-inflation accounting). The company's own primary 30.09.2026 summary financial statements PDF (via its investor-relations site) was read directly: amounts are presented at 30 September 2026 purchasing power, and the 2025 9M comparative column is restated to the SAME (September 2026) purchasing power - so the 9M2026 vs 9M2025 comparison is a genuine real comparison. The FY2025 full-year figure (on its own 31.12.2025 basis) is a different measuring unit; TTM was therefore not computed (see education.revenuePrevious).
researchTtrak.cashQuality: The primary 9M2026 report's cash flow statement (p.6) was read: the period net loss (789.3 million TL) coincided with operating cash flow of +5.02 billion TL - strong positive cash flow despite the net loss. This needs careful reading: most of it comes from a decrease in inventory (+2.82 billion TL, as production was cut faster than demand) and the depreciation add-back (+2.65 billion TL) - inventory drawdown is a one-off/temporary cash source, not a sign of sustainable earnings. "Cash flow beats profit, so the company is healthy" cannot be concluded.
researchTtrak.cashBridge: As of 30.09.2026, total financial debt is 13,133,877,360 TL (Note 6a short-term total 11,840,580,568 + Note 6b long-term total 1,293,296,792), cash and equivalents are 5,154,157,976 TL - net debt (debt minus cash) is -7,979,719,384 TL. The company is net-debt-positive (unlike YGGYO). All short-term bank loans are TL-denominated, at a 33.79% weighted-average effective rate; the EUR-denominated 19.5 million EUR long-term tranche is much cheaper at 5.35%. FX risk is limited but the TL interest cost is very high.
researchTtrak.growth: Revenue and operating profit were compared over the same nine-month period (1 January-30 September), on the same purchasing-power basis. Revenue: 36,737,705,425 TL (9M2025: 50,881,328,231 TL, real -27.80%); operating profit swung to a loss (-860,217,416 TL, 9M2025: +2,248,338,818 TL profit); period net loss 789,313,251 TL (9M2025: 1,189,261,639 TL profit). Gross margin fell from 14.69% to 9.40% - a profit decline proportionally larger than the revenue decline, a textbook operating-leverage effect. Since FY2025's full-year profit (565.4 million TL, own basis) was far below 9M2025's (1.19 billion TL), the downturn actually began in Q4 2025.
researchTtrak.peers: No direct one-to-one peer comparison was made in the industrial/automotive sector in this session. Turkey's tractor market itself (OSD data, -44% in the first 9 months of 2026) was used as the most direct contextual reference.
researchTtrak.dividend: Per the company's own official dividend-payment-history page: regular dividends were paid from 2007 to 2025 (more than one payment in some years); the most recent was 4,850,000,000 TL on 02.04.2025 (approximately 48.47 TL per share, derived by dividing by the 100,066,875 TL capital at that date). No payment record was found for 2026 to date. This is the distribution-decision calendar; it does not confirm that any payment reached a personal account.
researchTtrak.sustainability: There is a long dividend history, but given the 9M2026 loss and the net-debt position, a small or zero 2026 dividend is a plausible outcome (an inference, not a confirmed KAP decision). Because the borrowing-limit ratio is low, debt is not the main sustainability constraint; the main risk is the cyclical collapse in earnings power.
researchTtrak.valuation: For an industrial company, P/B and EV/EBITDA were used: book value per share (30.09.2026) is 199.28 TL, giving P/B 1.71x at the current price (341.75 TL) - this matches exactly across two independent sources (my own calculation and doviz.com). P/E cannot currently be computed (loss); using FY2025's (weak-year) profit gives P/E approximately 60.5x, which is not meaningful either. EV/EBITDA is approximately 17.7x, which looks high relative to the currently depressed EBITDA base, but a normalized multi-year EBITDA comparison could not be sourced in this session.

methods.pe: A current/TTM P/E cannot be computed because the company reported a loss in 9M2026 (negative EPS: -0.0789 TL/share). Using FY2025's (full-year, weak-year) net profit gives EPS of 5.6502 TL/share -> P/E of approximately 60.5x, but this figure is not a meaningful cheap/expensive signal either, because the reference earnings base was already inside the downturn (Q4 2025 was a loss) and a true TTM could not be produced due to the TAS 29 basis mismatch.
methods.ev: EV/EBITDA = (Market cap + Net debt) / EBITDA. 9M2026 EBITDA = operating loss (-860.2 million TL) + depreciation (2.65 billion TL) = 1.79 billion TL (margin 4.87%, a sharp drop from 9.68% in 9M2025). EV is approximately 42.18 billion TL. With a naive annualization (x4/3), EV/EBITDA is approximately 17.7x - high relative to the cyclical-trough EBITDA base; a normalized comparison is missing (see guide.missing).
methods.dcf: Multi-year tractor demand/price projections, an appropriate discount rate, and terminal-value assumptions could not be sourced in this session; no result is given.

scenarioNotes.bear: If Turkey's tractor market keeps shrinking into 2027 and the policy rate stays high, financing expense keeps weighing on profitability; once inventory drawdown is exhausted, operating cash flow could weaken too.
scenarioNotes.base: The market partially recovers from the 2026 trough in 2027, the rate environment improves gradually, export growth continues.
scenarioNotes.bull: The policy rate falls quickly, farmer financing eases, domestic demand rebounds fast, and operating leverage improves margins quickly. These conditions are not assumed to occur.

This observation is separate from the fundamental valuation analysis and does not imply a fair-value judgment.

Book value does not reflect every asset's current sale value; on its own this is not proof of cheap/expensive - the company reported a net loss in the same period, which should not be ignored when reading this ratio.
education.bookPerShare: 30 September 2026 equity (TRY 19,941,301,378) / 100,066,875 shares ~= TRY 199.28/share. This is the accounting value at the balance-sheet date; compared directly to the current price (TRY 341.75) it yields a P/B of 1.715x.
education.revenueGrowth: 9M 2026 revenue (TRY 36,737,705,425) vs 9M 2025 (TRY 50,881,328,231), same (September 2026) purchasing-power basis ~= -27.80% real. Consistent with the broad contraction of Turkey's tractor market, not a sign of a company-specific operational failure (see risks).
education.profitGrowth: 9M 2026 net loss (TRY 789,313,251) vs 9M 2025 net profit (TRY 1,189,261,639) is a swing from profit to loss; because the sign flips, the resulting percentage (around -166.37%) is a mathematical artifact, not a meaningful "growth rate". What matters is the absolute swing: roughly a TRY 1.98 billion profit-to-loss turnaround.
education.dividendYield: The company's own dividend-history page's most recent payment (02.04.2025, approx. TRY 48.4676/share) / current price (TRY 341.75) x 100 ~= 14.18%. Based on a past distribution decision (out of FY2024 profit); given the 9M2026 loss, there is no guarantee this rate repeats going forward.
education.operatingMargin: 9M 2026 operating loss (TRY 860,217,416) / revenue (TRY 36,737,705,425) x 100 ~= -2.34%. This margin was positive in the same period of 2025 (operating profit TRY 2,248,338,818) - it turned negative, a direct result of the market contraction.
education.currentRatio: 30 September 2026 current assets (TRY 22,034,025,190) / current liabilities (TRY 19,914,493,141) ~= 1.11x. Above 1 but a thin margin; most of current liabilities are trade payables and provisions rather than financial debt (see debtMeaning).
education.financialDebt: Short-term (TRY 11,840,580,568) + long-term (TRY 1,293,296,792) financial debt = TRY 13,133,877,360. The short-term portion's weight (~90% of the total) raises refinancing risk in a high TRY interest-rate environment (see interestMeaning).
education.cashProxy: Operating cash flow (TRY 5,023,848,014) minus capex (TRY 1,481,210,803) ~= TRY 3,542,637,211 free-cash-flow proxy. Despite reporting a net loss, the company appears to generate positive FCF; a significant part of this comes from working-capital/inventory drawdown, and should not be read as recurring cash generation (see cashQuality).
education.netDebt: Total financial debt (TRY 13,133,877,360) minus cash (TRY 5,154,157,976) = TRY 7,979,719,384 net debt (~TRY 8.0 billion). The company is net-debt; with EBITDA collapsed, a net-debt/EBITDA-style leverage ratio would not provide a meaningful comparison this period.
education.peHalfYear: This card compares market cap to the company's current-period net profit; TTRAK's current period in this report is the first NINE months of 2026 (not six), and it reported a net LOSS of TRY 789,313,251 for that period. P/E is mathematically undefined on negative/zero earnings, so it cannot be computed - this reflects a genuine loss, not missing data.
education.peRunRate: For the same reason (a 9M 2026 net loss), this scenario P/E also cannot be computed. The company was profitable in the same period of 2025 (TRY 1.19bn); the underlying picture is a swing from profit to loss, which a hypothetical annualization would not make more meaningful.

researchTtrak.debtMeaning: All short-term bank loans are TL-denominated (33.79% effective rate); a small part of the long-term loan (19.5 million EUR) is much cheaper at 5.35%. The 2.01 billion TL long-term TL loan that existed at 31.12.2025 was fully repaid by 30.09.2026. The result: most of the debt is expensive TL funding.
researchTtrak.interestMeaning: The weighted-average effective rate on TL loans is 33.79% (31.12.2025: 34.95%) - a direct reflection of Turkey's high policy-rate environment. This is the main driver of the large net financing expense (-2.84 billion TL) in 9M2026.
researchTtrak.fxMeaning: The company's revenue is largely TL-denominated (domestic) and EUR-denominated (exports); a small part of its debt is EUR-denominated. The FX-sensitivity table shows a relatively small net FX open position (in USD terms) - FX risk looks limited, but the full currency breakdown of assets/liabilities was not examined in depth in this session.
researchTtrak.cashRestrictions: Restricted-cash detail could not be additionally sourced in this session. The cash figure (5.15 billion TL) is taken from the "cash and cash equivalents" line of the primary financial statements; its components (restricted vs. free) could not be broken out.

guide.verdict: A market-leading, low-debt industrial company - but currently in a deep cyclical collapse (9M2026: a 789.3 million TL loss). A good company and good timing are not the same thing.
guide.reason: P/B (1.71x) on its own is neither extremely cheap nor expensive. EV/EBITDA (17.7x) looks high against the collapsed EBITDA base, but a normalized comparison is missing. P/E is currently meaningless (loss). These three mixed signals do not allow a single "cheap/expensive" verdict.
guide.business: Market leadership, low leverage, and export diversification are supportive. Whether Turkey's tractor market recovers in 2027, and the direction of the policy rate, are the two open questions.
guide.price: The share has lost 37% of its value over the past year - the market may have largely priced in the weakness, but this report cannot confidently conclude it is "now cheap" because the normalized earnings/EBITDA comparison is missing.
guide.decision: My current reading: NOT ASSESSED, due to mixed signals. No firm directional call should be expected before the market recovery and the rate environment become clearer.
guide.missingIntro: P/B could be computed, but some pieces are still missing for a full fair-value verdict:

missing.earnings: 1. A true TTM net profit: FY2025 and 9M2026/2025 are on different TAS 29 purchasing-power bases, so no conversion was possible; P/E is therefore unreliable.
missing.benchmark: 2. Normalized EBITDA: a same-basis multi-year EBITDA series could not be compiled in this session; the EV/EBITDA multiple rests only on the current (trough) period.
missing.cashflow: 3. The 2026 dividend decision: the company's own page shows no 2026 payment record; whether one was taken could not be confirmed.

guide.next: Once these inputs are available (FY2025 year-end statements, 2027 market data, the dividend decision), the distinction between a cyclical trough and a genuine valuation opportunity can be made more clearly.

backtest.explanationTitle: How should I read these percentages?
backtest.explanation: “Total return ÷ years” is the simple comparison you requested. For example, a 100% total gain over 10 years becomes 10% per year by this measure. It does not mean a 10% gain each year or a 10% compound annual return.
backtest.xirrExplanation: XIRR accounts for how long each contribution was invested. The first and last monthly payments are not treated as having the same holding period. This is a better annual performance measure for recurring investments. Dividends are already included in ending value; do not add them again.
backtest.method: $83.33 is invested on each month’s last trading day, and $83.37 every twelfth month, totaling exactly $1,000 per year. Shares are bought using that day’s FX. Dividend entitlement is based on shares held before the ex-date, with reinvestment on the payment date or next trading day. Entitled but unpaid dividends at cutoff are included as receivables, not as reinvested shares.
backtest.formulas: Shares purchased = USD contribution × FX ÷ price. Dividend shares = gross entitlement ÷ payment-date price. Ending value = (shares × closing price + dividend receivable) ÷ ending FX. Total return = (ending value − contributions) ÷ contributions × 100. Simple annual average = total return ÷ years.
backtest.limits: Prices and dividends use the same split-adjusted basis; splits are not applied again. Total-return adjusted close is not used, avoiding double-counted dividends. Fractional shares, no fees and gross dividends are comparison assumptions. Stock and FX daily closes may occur at different times; FX holidays use the latest available rate within four calendar days. Inflation, taxes, spreads and actual execution prices are excluded. Past performance may not repeat.
backtest.review: Approximate research calculation; source review is partial and performed by the same agent. The September 2023 TUPRS dividend discrepancy was corrected using the company report. The 2008 final distribution in Is Yatirim was used instead of the initial proposal; the provider’s second entry was not added. Historical payment dates use a secondary calendar; not every KAP attachment was individually verified.

researchFroto.name: Ford Otosan
researchFroto.sector: Automotive · Passenger/commercial vehicle and tractor manufacturing
researchFroto.headline: Low leverage, a 26-year unbroken dividend payer — but H1 2026 profit fell a real 40% on European demand weakness
researchFroto.summary: Ford Otosan is a joint venture between Ford Motor Company (41.04%) and Koc Holding (39.32%); it builds passenger/commercial vehicles and tractors at its Kocaeli, Eskisehir and Craiova (Romania) plants, exporting mainly to Europe. This report works from the H1 2026 interim statements, the company’s own disclosed Net Financial Debt/EBITDA ratio, and its FY2021-2025 profit history; the price looks reasonable against the genuine TTM P/E (7.3x), but the real 40% drop in H1 profit should not be ignored.
researchFroto.strengths: Net Financial Debt/Adjusted EBITDA of 1.76x (30.06.2026, company-disclosed, well below its own 3.5x target); FY2025 ROE of 22.2%; P/B of 1.36x (reasonable); 26 years of uninterrupted dividend payments (since 2005); a new proposed cash dividend (TRY 2.6095/share) on 27.10.2026; large production capacity and a European export network.
researchFroto.risks: H1 2026 revenue fell 11.5% and net profit fell 39.8% in real terms (European demand contraction and cost pressure); operating margin dropped to just 2.7%; a 10:1 bonus share issue in 2025 multiplied the share count tenfold (valuation multiples must be read accordingly); Q3 results are not yet published (due 5 November 2026); the proposed TRY 2.6095/share dividend has not yet been approved at the Extraordinary General Meeting (24.11.2026), payment date unknown.
researchFroto.accounting: Consolidated interim figures under TAS 29 (high-inflation accounting). The company’s own 30.06.2026 primary consolidated interim statements (from its investor relations site) were read directly: all amounts are expressed in 30 June 2026 purchasing power, and the H1 2025 and 1 Jan 2025/2026 opening-balance comparatives are restated to the SAME (June 2026) purchasing power — so the H1 2026 vs H1 2025 comparison and the FY2025 average-equity calculation are genuine real comparisons; different TAS29 bases from separate sources were not mixed.
researchFroto.cashQuality: H1 2026 operating cash flow was TRY 19,219,209 thousand while net profit was TRY 10,336,713 thousand — cash generation is about 1.86x reported profit. Depreciation (TRY 10,403,700 thousand) and working-capital movements (including a trade-payables increase) drive this gap; the same ratio was higher in H1 2025 (83.8/17.2≈4.9x) — the relative weakening in cash generation is consistent with the profit decline.
researchFroto.cashBridge: As of 30.06.2026 total financial debt was TRY 168,024,403 thousand (short 57,626,834 + long 110,397,569), cash and equivalents TRY 56,042,423 thousand — net financial debt TRY 111,981,980 thousand (matches the company’s own figure exactly). The company tracks its capital structure via "Net Financial Debt/Adjusted EBITDA" (1.76x, target ≤3.5x); Adjusted EBITDA (trailing four quarters) is TRY 63,557,627 thousand — a genuine TTM figure the company discloses itself, not something we had to construct.
researchFroto.growth: Revenue and profit were compared over the same six-month period (1 Jan-30 Jun), on the same purchasing-power basis. Revenue TRY 427,069,180 thousand (H1 2025: 482,673,106 thousand, real −11.52%); net profit TRY 10,336,713 thousand (H1 2025: 17,157,738 thousand, real −39.75%). Operating profit was TRY 11,645,149 thousand (H1 2025: 26,724,288 thousand, real −56.42%) — the operating-margin squeeze explains most of the net profit decline; it is not a one-off item.
researchFroto.peers: No direct multiple comparison against other BIST automotive names (e.g. TOASO, TTRAK) was done in this session; FROTO’s export-weighted (European) model and its Ford/Koc joint-venture structure are noted as a structural difference from other BIST automotive names.
researchFroto.dividend: A cash dividend has been paid every year from 2005 to 2026 (excluding the pre-redenomination era); the last payment was on 2026-02-28 (TRY 3.64/share, based on the 2025 decision). On 27.10.2026 a new proposal (net TRY 2.6095/share) was disclosed to KAP; the Extraordinary General Meeting on 24.11.2026 will approve it — as of this report it has NOT yet been paid, payment date unknown (see Data gaps). At the current price (TRY 69.20) the proposed dividend implies a 3.77% yield.
researchFroto.sustainability: A 26-year unbroken dividend record is a strong signal. Net Financial Debt/EBITDA (1.76x) is well below the company’s own 3.5x target, so debt risk does not threaten dividend sustainability. The main risk: H1 2026 net profit fell a real 40%; if this continues, future dividend growth could slow, though the current cash/debt structure comfortably supports the present payout level.
researchFroto.valuation: Reference market value (price x shares) is TRY 242,829,720,000. On genuine TTM net profit (FY2025 + H1 2026 − H1 2025 = TRY 33,200,368 thousand, same purchasing-power basis) P/E ≈ 7.31x — a reasonable level for the automotive sector. P/B is 1.36x, book value per share TRY 51.06. EV/EBITDA (using the company’s own disclosed TTM EBITDA) ≈ 5.58x, Net Debt/EBITDA 1.76x (matches the company’s own figure exactly).

methods.pe: A genuine TTM P/E could be computed: FY2025 full-year net profit (TRY 40,021,393 thousand, from this report’s own equity-change statement, June 2026 basis) + H1 2026 (10,336,713) − H1 2025 (17,157,738) = TRY 33,200,368 thousand TTM profit. P/E = 242,829,720,000 / 33,200,368,000 ≈ 7.31x. This is a genuine trailing-12-month reconstruction, not a naive annualization.
methods.ev: For EV/EBITDA, the company’s OWN disclosed Adjusted EBITDA (trailing 4 quarters, TRY 63,557,627 thousand) and Net Financial Debt (TRY 111,981,980 thousand) were used — not separately calculated for this report, taken directly from the primary source. EV = Market cap + Net debt = TRY 354,811,700,000; EV/EBITDA ≈ 5.58x.
methods.dcf: A multi-year free-cash-flow projection, an appropriate discount rate and terminal-value assumptions could not be sourced in this session; no result.

researchIsmen.name: İş Yatırım Menkul Değerler
researchIsmen.headline: Core commission income held up (-4.1%), but H1 2026 net profit fell 35.2% because 2025's one-off investment gain did not repeat
researchIsmen.summary: This report uses P/B and ROE methods appropriate for the brokerage sector (instead of EV/EBITDA used for industrials). Eight periods (2021-2026) were read from the company's own Mali Tablolar tool (Matriks data). Price is close to book value on a P/B basis (~1.07x); ROE (~24.0% on a latest-full-year basis) is strong, but most of the H1 2026 profit decline stems from a one-off 2025 investment gain that did not recur, not from operational deterioration.
researchIsmen.strengths: Core commission/fee/interest income fell only -4.1% in H1 2026 vs H1 2025 (TRY 13.76bn vs TRY 14.34bn) — the core brokerage business was largely preserved; ROE on an FY2025 basis is ~24.0% (strong); an unbroken, growing cash dividend history since 2008 (TRY 3.1667/share in 2026); P/B (~1.07x) is close to book, not richly premium; backing of the İş Bankası group and a long-established position on BIST (listed since 2007).
researchIsmen.risks: H1 2026 net profit (parent share) was TRY 2.617bn, down -35.2% from H1 2025's TRY 4.038bn; a significant part of this decline stems from a one-off TRY 2.49bn 'investment activity income' line in H1 2025 that dropped to zero in H1 2026 (see growth); the share price has fallen ~-47.6% from its 52-week high (TRY 48.16, January 2026) to today (TRY 25.22); Q3 (9-month) results have not yet been published per the KAP calendar (expected window 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-09); a 'commission-only' breakdown could not be isolated this session, the figure used is a combined interest+fee+commission line.
researchIsmen.accounting: Data were read from the company's own isyatirim.com.tr 'Mali Tablolar' tool (Series XI No:29 template, Matriks Financial Technologies data); although the page header says 'non-consolidated', the table shows a minority-interest/parent-equity split, so this report tags scope as CONSOLIDATED (this may be a template artifact). This aggregator is not KAP's primary XBRL/PDF document; the figures are time-consistent with the H1 2026 KAP filing date (~12 August 2026) but the filing itself was not separately read this session (see Data gaps). The aggregator does not state an explicit TMS 29 purchasing-power date, so the accounting field is tagged NOMINAL; the H1 2026 vs H1 2025 comparison is therefore not a 'real' (inflation-adjusted) comparison, just a comparison of two periods' own nominal TRY amounts (the 12-month inflation effect is small but non-zero).
researchIsmen.growth: The income statement was compared over the same six-month period (1 January-30 June). Net profit (parent share) was TRY 2,616,705,000 (H1 2025: TRY 4,037,753,000, -35.2%); the core 'interest, fee, premium, commission and other income' line was TRY 13,757,995,000 (H1 2025: TRY 14,341,956,000, -4.1%) — core income stayed nearly flat while net profit fell far more sharply. Most of the gap comes from the income statement's 'investment activity income' line: TRY 0 in H1 2026 vs TRY 2,489,755,000 in H1 2025 (and this amount is nearly identical to the full-year FY2025 figure — i.e. all of it occurred within H1 2025, a one-off). This single line alone explains roughly two-thirds of the pre-tax profit gap between the two periods (TRY 3.90bn).
researchIsmen.peers: No direct, like-for-like multiple comparison with another brokerage was made this session. Its position within the İş Bankası group (see company.ownership) is the closest structural reference.
researchIsmen.dividend: Per the company's own Dividends table (2008-2026): an uninterrupted gross cash dividend was paid every year, rising from TRY 0.0796/share in 2008 to TRY 3.1667/share in 2026 (intervening amounts are not directly comparable due to repeated bonus share issuances, see backtest.review). The latest payment was on 2026-04-01; at the current price (TRY 25.22) the gross yield is ~12.56%. This is the distribution decision's calendar; it does not confirm payment into any personal account.
researchIsmen.sustainability: There is an uninterrupted, long dividend history; FY2025 ROE (~24.0%) is strong enough to support it. The main risk is whether the H1 2026 profit decline — mostly a one-off investment-income loss — drags down full-year 2026 profit and therefore the dividend proposed in 2027; this is an inference, not a confirmed KAP decision.
researchIsmen.valuation: P/B and ROE were used for the brokerage sector: reference market cap (TRY 25.22 x 1,500,000,000 shares) is TRY 37,830,000,000; against 30 June 2026 parent equity (TRY 35,252,706,000), P/B is ~1.073x — very close to book value, neither clearly discounted nor premium. ROE was computed on an FY2025 annualFallback basis rather than a true TTM (rationale: H1 2025 profit was not separately pulled for a flow reconstruction, so the single metricKey:'profit'-tagged full year was used): FY2025 net profit (TRY 8,767,628,073) / average equity ((38,133,598,540+34,829,493,175)/2 = TRY 36,481,545,858) ~ 24.03%.

methods.pe: A P/E was not computed for the broker profile (BOOK_ROE method); the company's own Finansal Oranlar tab shows P/E=5.1 for the 6/2026 period, but its full calculation trail (which earnings base, which price date) was not reproduced this session, so it was not included in this report's own figures (see Data gaps).
methods.ev: EV/EBITDA does not apply to a brokerage (per CLAUDE.md, industrial-company logic is not applied to financial institutions); P/B and ROE were used instead (see valuation).
methods.dcf: A multi-year commission income/trading volume projection, a suitable discount rate and terminal-value assumptions could not be sourced this session; there is no computed result.

researchIsmen.scenarios: The following are not numeric price targets, but conditions to research.

scenarioNotes.bear: If BIST trading volumes keep shrinking through H2 2026, core commission income could start declining too; without a one-off investment gain like 2025's, full-year 2026 profit could end up well below FY2025.
scenarioNotes.base: Core commission income continues near the H1 2026 run-rate (roughly -4% y/y), and Q3 results (expected 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-09) come in consistent with the H1 trend.
scenarioNotes.bull: BIST trading volumes recover and/or a new one-off investment/associate gain materializes, bringing full-year profit closer to the FY2025 level. This is not assumed to occur.

researchIsmen.technical: Per Yahoo Finance's monthly close data (2007-2026), the stock traded in a TRY 25.12-48.16 range over the last 52 weeks, with the current price (TRY 25.22) very close to the bottom of that range. This observation is kept separate from fundamental valuation (P/B, ROE) and carries no fair-value judgment.
researchIsmen.scanLimit: KAP's own detailed query interface could not be reached this session; İş Yatırım's own Mali Tablolar/Finansal Oranlar tool (Matriks data, the company's own site) was used as the primary source. The H1 2026 results' KAP filing date (~12 August 2026) was corroborated by secondary news aggregators (bigpara, vkyanaliz), but the exact KAP filing number was not identified this session. That Q3 (9-month) results have not yet been published was confirmed via KAP's own filing-calendar page. "No other material disclosure" cannot be inferred; coverage is PARTIAL.
researchIsmen.riskFollowup: Next update should check: the 2026 Q3 (9-month) financial statements (expected 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-09), whether full-year 2026 profit actually falls short of or matches FY2025, and the relationship between commission income and BIST trading volumes.
researchIsmen.review: Research and review were done by the same agent in a separate pass; this is not an independent audit. Identity and financial figures were read from the company's own Mali Tablolar tool (Matriks data), a different reliability tier from reading KAP's primary document directly (see accounting). P/B, ROE and dividend yield were reproduced from this data. KAP scanning is PARTIAL, the 'commission-only' breakdown and Q3 results are missing — for these reasons the review outcome is NEEDS_REVIEW; this report is partial research.

researchToaso.name: Tofaş
researchToaso.sector: Automotive · Fiat/Stellantis-licensed passenger and light commercial vehicle manufacturing
researchToaso.headline: Strong real revenue/profit growth and a TTM P/E of 7.5x look reasonable — but H1 2026 inventory build pulled operating cash flow deeply negative, worth watching
researchToaso.summary: Tofaş is an equal joint venture between Koç Holding (37.62%) and Stellantis Europe S.p.A. (37.86%); it manufactures passenger and light commercial vehicles under Fiat/Stellantis license at its Bursa plant for domestic sale and export. This report works from the 30 June 2026 interim condensed consolidated financial statements, the 2025 Integrated Annual Report, and a genuine TTM profit derived from the statement of changes in equity; the price looks reasonable on a real TTM P/E (~7.5x) and EV/EBITDA (~13.9x) basis, but H1 2026’s large inventory build pulled free cash flow deeply negative.
researchToaso.strengths: H1 2026 revenue grew a real 60.6%, net profit a real 197% (operating profit swung from an H1 2025 loss to an H1 2026 profit); genuine TTM P/E ~7.5x, P/B ~1.61x — not aggressive multiples for the automotive sector; genuine TTM-aligned ROE 21.64% (based on the average of equity at 30.06.2026 and 30.06.2025; the company's own FY2025 report states a different ROE of 13.9% using a different period/denominator); dividend yield (net 17.00 TL/share) 8.05% at the current price; over 50 years of continuous production/export history and strong joint-venture backing from Koç Holding and Stellantis.
researchToaso.risks: In H1 2026 inventory jumped from 19.8bn TL to 43.4bn TL (+23.5bn TL); as a result operating cash flow turned to -7.2bn TL and the free-cash-flow proxy to -11.6bn TL — a clear warning that reported profit has not yet converted to cash; short-term financial debt rose from 19.1bn TL to 29.6bn TL (inventory financing); the current ratio fell to 1.50; Net Debt/EBITDA (FY2025 basis) is ~3.4x; Q3 (9-month) results are not yet published (5 November 2026); a conflict was found between the primary-source PDF text extraction and market data on share count, resolved in favor of market data (see data gaps).
researchToaso.accounting: Consolidated, TAS 29 (high-inflation accounting) interim figures. The company's own 30 June 2026 interim condensed consolidated statements were read directly via KAP: all amounts are presented at 30 June 2026 purchasing power, and the H1 2025 and opening 1 Jan 2025/2026 balances (including FY2024 and FY2025 closings) have been restated to the SAME (June 2026) purchasing power - so the H1 2026 vs H1 2025 comparison, the genuine TTM profit reconstruction, and the 30.06.2025->30.06.2026 average-equity (ROE) calculation are all consistent real comparisons. EBITDA and net debt (for the FY2025 full-year EV/EBITDA card) are a deliberate EXCEPTION, taken from the 2025 Integrated Annual Report's own (31 Dec 2025) purchasing-power basis - the two sources were not mixed (see methods.ev).
researchToaso.cashQuality: H1 2026 operating cash flow was -7,202,222 thousand TL while period profit was +6,290,532 thousand TL - cash generation moved in the OPPOSITE direction from profit. Depreciation (2,982,637 thousand TL) helped, but the change in working capital (chiefly a 23,519,804 thousand TL inventory increase) outweighed it by far. H1 2025 operating cash flow was +17,094,892 thousand TL (about 8x profit) - the direction reversed completely, an important earnings-quality warning.
researchToaso.cashBridge: As of 30 June 2026 total financial debt was 70,364,733 thousand TL (short 29,574,156 + long 40,790,577), cash and equivalents 11,008,676 thousand TL - current net debt 59,356,057 thousand TL. For the EV/EBITDA and Net Debt/EBITDA cards, the company's OWN FY2025 figures from its 2025 Integrated Annual Report were used instead (full year, 31 Dec 2025 purchasing-power basis): net financial debt 33,701,681 thousand TL, EBITDA ~10.0bn TL (the board report's own summary table, rounded to one decimal) - Net Debt/EBITDA ~3.37x, consistent with secondary sources' reported 3.4x.
researchToaso.growth: Revenue and profit were compared over the same six-month period (1 Jan-30 Jun), on the same purchasing-power basis. Revenue 201,797,108 thousand TL (H1 2025: 125,633,352 thousand TL, real +60.62%); net profit 6,290,532 thousand TL (H1 2025: 2,116,615 thousand TL, real +197.26%); operating profit 2,884,353 thousand TL (H1 2025: a loss of -879,779 thousand TL, i.e. a swing from loss to profit) - growth appears to come from both revenue and operating-margin improvement, though it has not yet shown up in cash flow (see cashQuality).
researchToaso.peers: No direct multiple comparison against other BIST automotive names (e.g. FROTO, TTRAK) was done in this session; Tofaş's Fiat/Stellantis-licensed manufacturing model and the Koç+Stellantis joint-venture structure are noted as a structural difference from other BIST automotive names.
researchToaso.dividend: Regular cash dividends were paid from 2005 through 2026; the most recent payment was on 2026-02-28 (gross 20.00 TL / net 17.00 TL per share, from FY2025 profit, confirmed against the 2025 Integrated Annual Report's dividend distribution table). The prior payment was 2025-04-07 (gross 12.00 TL / net 10.20 TL per share, from FY2024 profit). At the current price (211.20 TL) the yield on the last paid net dividend is 8.05%.
researchToaso.sustainability: A continuous, multi-year dividend history is a strong signal. The FY2025 Net Debt/EBITDA (~3.4x) should be read together with the company's own reported rise in Total Financial Debt/Equity (59.2%->89.4%) - leverage increased materially versus 2024. The main risk: if the large H1 2026 inventory build and negative operating cash flow persist, future dividend capacity could end up funded by borrowing rather than operating profit; the current cash position (11.0bn TL) alone is not reassuring.
researchToaso.valuation: Reference market cap (price x shares) is 105,600,000,000 TL. On genuine TTM net profit (FY2025 + H1 2026 - H1 2025 = 14,011,341 thousand TL, same purchasing-power basis) P/E is ~7.54x - a low/reasonable level for the automotive sector. P/B is 1.606x, book value per share 131.48 TL. EV/EBITDA (using the company's own FY2025 EBITDA disclosure) is ~13.93x, Net Debt/EBITDA ~3.37x.

methods.pe: A genuine TTM P/E could be computed: FY2025 full-year net profit (9,837,424 thousand TL, from this report's own statement of changes in equity "Transfers" line, on the June 2026 basis) + H1 2026 (6,290,532) - H1 2025 (2,116,615) = 14,011,341 thousand TL TTM profit. P/E = 105,600,000,000 / 14,011,341,000 ~ 7.54x. This is a genuine trailing-12-month reconstruction, not a naive annualization (all inputs share the same 30 June 2026 purchasing-power basis).
methods.ev: Because EV/EBITDA and Net Debt/EBITDA need full-year data, and the H1 2026 report does not restate FY2025 EBITDA, the company's OWN 2025 Integrated Annual Report FY2025 figures (original 31 Dec 2025 purchasing-power basis) were used instead: EBITDA ~10.0bn TL (board report summary table), net financial debt 33,701,681 thousand TL (current portion of long-term borrowings + long-term borrowings - cash, from the same FY2025 report). EV = market cap + net debt = 139,301,681,000 TL; EV/EBITDA ~13.93x. This is a deliberate mixed-period choice (price current, debt/EBITDA as of FY2025 year-end) because the H1 2026 report does not restate full-year EBITDA; the two TAS29 bases were not mixed with each other (each stayed within its own internally-consistent set).
methods.dcf: A multi-year free-cash-flow projection with a suitable discount rate and terminal-value assumptions could not be sourced in this session; no computed result.

guide.verdict: An automotive manufacturer with rapidly growing real revenue/profit, reasonably priced on a genuine TTM P/E (7.5x) - but H1 2026's large inventory build pulled operating cash flow deeply negative, a trend to watch in Q3.
guide.reason: Because a genuine trailing-12-month (TTM) net profit could be computed, the P/E is based on a FY2025 + H1 2026 - H1 2025 reconstruction rather than a naive annualization. guide.business: A Koç Holding + Stellantis Europe joint venture, Fiat/Stellantis-licensed manufacturing; in H1 2026 revenue grew a real 60.6%, net profit a real 197%, and operating profit swung from a loss to a profit. The main risk: in the same period inventory rose by 23.5bn TL and operating cash flow fell to -7.2bn TL - profit growth has not yet converted to cash.

researchPagyo.summary: Panora earns rent and service income from its Ankara shopping centre and holds land with development potential. H1 revenue was TRY671.01m and profit TRY424.35m. The TRY113 close implies a 44.70% discount to book NAV and 5.35x trailing P/E. Current appraisal/occupancy and conflicting valuation assumptions remain unresolved; these ratios alone do not establish undervaluation.
researchPagyo.strengths: Rent grew 5.97% on the same purchasing-power basis; operating cash was TRY488.32m. Cash of TRY278.47m exceeds bank debt of TRY190,812, but TRY222m of interest-bearing land payables must also be considered.
researchPagyo.risks: Income is concentrated in one Ankara mall. Tenant collections, retail demand, land-development costs and instalments bearing 24% interest matter. The H1 activity report states no material litigation for that period, not a complete legal clearance through October. Appraisal occupancy of 91% and the 97–98% assumptions in the financial note are not equivalent measures.
researchPagyo.accounting: Consolidated figures are in TRY, not thousands, at June 2026 purchasing power. Property of TRY19.167bn comprises indexed 2025 appraisal value of 19.165bn plus 1.936m additions, not a new June appraisal. Nominal 2021/22 and IAS29 2023 annual profits have different measurement bases.
researchPagyo.cashBridge: Narrow financial debt is TRY190,812 of bank loans; net debt after cash is −278,274,394. Including TRY222m interest-bearing land payables gives economic debt of 222,190,812 and net cash of 56,274,394. Land payables and deferred tax of TRY1.492bn are already deducted in NAV; do not deduct them twice.
researchPagyo.cashQuality: Operating cash 488,323,041 less capex 10,667,318 gives TRY477,655,723, covering 92.88% of H1 dividends of 514,250,404 on the same purchasing-power basis. Adding 69,628,724 interest received and deducting 33,213 loan repayments gives 547,251,234, or 106.42% coverage. Future land principal/interest payments still need budgeting; this is no dividend guarantee.
researchPagyo.growth: Revenue grew 5.95% and rent 5.97%, while net profit fell 2.45%. The monetary result moved from a TRY65.01m gain to a 30.82m loss. Operating cash declined from 543.61m to 488.32m. Rental growth does not imply that all earnings and cash measures improved.
researchPagyo.peers: İş Yatırım’s roughly 5.4x P/E and 0.6x P/B are close to the recalculated ratios, not an independent fair value. The dated Vakıf report returned 404. No aligned mall-REIT peer set with consistent appraisal, tax and rent scope was established, so no target multiple is assigned.
